title: GPU CUDA NCCL upgrade validation checklist (2026 Q1 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft checklist and validation notes for Kubernetes + GPU driver / CUDA / NCCL upgrades in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: minimize downtime for inference fleets, validate runtime correctness, and capture Terraform module changes required for kubelet/driver lifecycle automation.

Context and goals:
- We have a set of Dedicated/private clusters running mixed NVIDIA Ampere/RTX compute. Planned upgrade window: Q1 2026 to align with provider driver releases.
- Validate combination matrix for K8s nodes, NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkits and NCCL used by inference workloads.
- Produce an automated test harness and a manual smoke checklist to run during upgrade windows.
- Capture required Terraform module changes (node pool tagging, taints, upgrade_strategy variables).

Scope (what this doc covers):
- On-prem and cloud VPC private clusters managed by our private control plane.
- Kubernetes node OS: Ubuntu 22.04 and RHEL 9 (notes for both).
- GPU families: A10/A100/A30 and newer Ampere/Blackwell where applicable.
- Drivers: 515.x -> 540.x -> 550.x series (we test specific versions below).
- CUDA: 11.7, 11.8, 12.1 (major workloads currently pinned to 11.8).
- NCCL: 2.14, 2.16, 2.17.

Quick compatibility matrix (summary; full matrix artifacts live in Confluence):
Columns: k8s | distro | nvidia-driver | cuda | nccl | expected notes
- k8s 1.25 | Ubuntu22.04 | 515.105 | 11.7 | 2.14 | legacy; acceptable but no new features
- k8s 1.26 | Ubuntu22.04 | 535.86 | 11.8 | 2.16 | recommended for current RL workloads (passes e2e smoke)
- k8s 1.27 | Ubuntu22.04 | 540.30 | 12.1 | 2.17 | emerging; requires container/tooling rebuild for some images
- k8s 1.27 | RHEL9 | 540.30 | 11.8 | 2.16 | mixed; validate libc compatibility on RHEL image builds
- k8s 1.28 (test) | Ubuntu22.04 | 550.10 | 12.1 | 2.17 | experimental (test only)

Validation test plan (high level):
1) Node-level sanity (per node):
   - Check kernel and driver: uname -r; modinfo nvidia | head -n 5; sudo cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log (if present)
   - Verify nvidia-smi output and affinity: docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi
   - Kube-level: kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | grep -i nvidia
2) Device plugin and kubelet integration:
   - Confirm Device Plugin DaemonSet is running and healthy: kubectl -n kube-system get ds nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
   - Logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --tail=200
   - Test scheduling: deploy simple pod requesting nvidia.com/gpu:1 and ensure it runs and outputs nvidia-smi
3) Workload smoke tests (per workload type):
   - Model inference (quantized small model): 1000 requests, observe p50/p95 latency regression <= 15%
   - Large model end-to-end: run one sample 8k token generation trough pipeline; sanity-check output correctness (prompt-to-prompt checksum for deterministic models)
   - Multi-GPU NCCL test: run NCCL all-reduce benchmark across 2 nodes and capture bandwidth and error rates
4) End-to-end CI job (automated):
   - Pipeline runs in test project: terraform apply test cluster -> run terraform module tests -> deploy device-plugin -> execute smoke jobs -> capture logs/artifacts

Terraform module notes (summary of required changes):
- new variables to add: gpu_driver_version (string), cuda_version (string), driver_install_method (package|runfile|dkms), preemptible_compatible (bool)
- node_pool lifecycle: add create_before_destroy where possible to enable rolling replacement with temporary capacity pools
- taint-based draining: add default gpu_upgrade_taint = { key = "maintenance", value = "true", effect = "NoSchedule" } and documentation for drain flow
- example snippet: 
   module "gpu_node_pool" {
     source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//k8s-gpu-nodepool"
     instance_count = 3
     node_labels = { "node.kubernetes.io/gpu" = "true" }
     gpu_driver_version = var.gpu_driver_version
     post_install_script = file("modules/gpu/scripts/validate-driver.sh")
   }
- test plan for Terraform changes: run plan -> apply in staging -> assert node labels and driver installed via SSH or daemonset probe -> simulate upgrade via changing gpu_driver_version and applying with max_unavailable = 1

Upgrade runbook (abridged):
- PRE-UPGRADE (48h):
  - Collect baseline: node metrics (GPU utilization, temperature), serving latencies, token costs per model. Export to S3/test-report/<date>/baseline.json
  - Notify impacted teams and set maintenance pages, escalation contacts
- DRY-RUN (staging cluster):
  - Apply terraform changes in staging, run full smoke tests and NCCL benchmarks, collect artifacts
  - Confirm images compatible (rebuild images with new CUDA if needed)
- UPGRADE (production rolling):
  - For each AZ or rack: cordon -> drain (respect GPU eviction time) -> delete node / scale-in replacement nodes with driver preinstalled -> wait until Ready and device-plugin healthy -> run workload smoke on new node -> uncordon cluster segment
  - Monitor: 5m heartbeats, job traces, prometheus GPU exporter metrics, error logs; rollback if any p95 latency spike > 30% sustained for 15m or any OOMs on inference containers
- POST-UPGRADE: run full regression test, snapshot logs, mark change in change-log, and schedule follow-up postmortem if any incidents

Smoke test checklist (run during and after each node replacement):
- [ ] Node Ready state within 5m of kubelet start
- [ ] device-plugin DaemonSet registers GPUs within 3m after kubelet ready
- [ ] nvidia-smi inside pod returns expected driver and memory info
- [ ] Inference job runs and returns baseline-percentiles within threshold
- [ ] NCCL all-reduce completes without error and bandwidth within 80% of baseline
- [ ] No CSI or storage errors observed on pods that use PVs

Rollback criteria / plan:
- Immediate rollback triggers: kernel oops, repeated node reboots, NCCL process failures, OOM kills > 5% of pods in pool
- Rollback steps: scale up previous node template (driver pinned to previous version) -> wait for healthy -> migrate workloads -> drain and decommission failing nodes

Common failure modes we've seen (notes to add to runbooks):
- Driver package mismatch with kernel headers on RHEL -> leads to module build failure; workaround: ensure kernel-debuginfo/header package pinned with terraform pre-boot script
- Container glibc mismatches after CUDA bump -> some python wheels compiled against older toolchain fail; need to rebuild wheel manylinux images or pin CUDA runtime in container
- NCCL hang on cross-AZ traffic with older versions (2.14) when MTU <= 9000; ensure jumbo frames where possible or upgrade NCCL

Acceptance criteria for promoting to production (must pass all):
- 95% of smoke runs pass in staging for 72h continuous testing
- No p95 latency regression > 20% in synthetic traffic test for any model group
- Terraform changes merged with module tests and reviewed: PR #88 acceptance (see linked artifact)

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize on driver_install_method = runfile for all on-prem? (Pros: reproducible; Cons: slower installs and fewer distro package benefits)
- Confirm compatibility with upcoming Blackwell GPUs — who will own test hardware procurement? (tag: @hardware-ops)
- Add automation to detect rogue nodes that still have older drivers post-upgrade.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Export full CSV matrix into Confluence (I will generate via compatibility-matrix-generator job).
- Build a tiny k8s job that runs cuda/nccl microbenchmarks automatically after node Ready and attach logs to terraform apply output in CI.

References / commands of interest:
- Verify device plugin: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=nvidia-device-plugin -o wide
- Quick driver test: docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
- NCCL test: git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests && ./build.sh && mpirun -np 4 ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2

End of draft.
